# A perspective captured while a pane is torn out restores without it

## Context

Found on the Fleet Manager cockpit (neomjs/neo-agent-institution#127, live through the Neural Link on 2026-09-12): the inspector was popped out into its own window, `capture_perspective` (window scope) stored a layout, the pane came home, and restoring that layout took the inspector out of the window. It stays unreachable until another perspective is restored. Intake of that ticket found the cause on the engine's side of the line, in the read both capture producers share.

Measured at dev@cca529ecff with a real `dock.Workspace` (`enableDockTearOutLifecycle: true`), `applyTearOutOperation({operation: 'detachItem', itemId: 'preview'})`, then `Persistence.capturePerspective(workspace.getDockZoneDocument(), …)`:

```
catalogKeepsPreview : true
recordPlacesPreview : null
ownerHoldsHome      : {tabsNodeId: 'side-tabs', index: 0, home: {parentId: 'root-split', slot: 1, …}}
```

## The Problem

A window-scope capture records `getDockZoneDocument()` as it is. While a pane is away in a vessel the document keeps its catalog record and no placement — `detachItem` removed it — and that is exactly how the document spells a CLOSED pane (the declared-but-unplaced shape, settled in Discussion `#18468`). So the record says "this perspective has no inspector", although the pane was never closed: it was elsewhere, and the workspace knew where it lives. The document alone cannot tell the two apart. The tear-out owner can — it holds the recorded home of every pane it took out.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs:1039-1045` — `applyTearOutOperation` captures the pre-detach placement (`WorkspaceDocument.captureItemPlacement`) and hands it to the tear-out owner (`recordPlacement`).
- `src/dashboard/dock/window/TearOut.mjs:123-126` — `placements` is that record; `:321-337` read it without consuming (`placements`, `peekPlacement`), `:486-491` the return consumes it.
- `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs:1195-1201` — `resolveDockReturnDescriptor(document, itemId, placement)` lowers a recorded home to the `restoreTab` descriptor the return applies.
- `src/ai/client/DockService.mjs:327` — the Neural Link capture is `Persistence.capturePerspective(this.readDocument(holder), metadata)`; `readDocument` (`:222-224`) is `holder.getDockZoneDocument()`, which answers `dockModel` (`Workspace.mjs:2312`).
- A host's own capture verb reads the same accessor (the cockpit: `CockpitPerspectives.captureSavedLayout(view.getDockZoneDocument(), …)`).
- The restore side already composes: `TearOut.mjs:546-557` treats an item the document places while its pane is still away as "already in the tree" and only re-projects on the return, and a host's `resolvePane` can hold the slot meanwhile (the cockpit answers a stand-in).

## The Fix

`dock.Workspace` gets the read a window-scope capture wants: the committed document with every pane the tear-out owner holds a home for folded back into that home — through the same descriptor and reducer the return uses (`resolveDockReturnDescriptor` → `Operations.applyOperation`), over the document value, never over `dockModel`. The fold asks the return's own two questions: the recorded home first, then the host's answer for a home that is gone (`resolveDockReturnDescriptor(document, itemId, null)`); a fold the reducer refuses under both leaves that item as the live document has it. A pane the document already places while it is away — a perspective restored while the vessel stands — stays where the document has it. `DockService#capturePerspective` reads it for `captureScope: 'window'`; a holder without it keeps `readDocument`. Topology scope stays as it is: there the vessel's workspace is part of the record and places the pane itself.

Working name: `getPerspectiveDocument()`.

## Contract Ledger

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Neo.dashboard.dock.Workspace#getPerspectiveDocument()` (new) | this ticket | the committed document with vessel-held panes folded into their recorded homes; a pure read | a fold the reducer refuses leaves the item unplaced | JSDoc | unit arm |
| `Neo.ai.client.DockService#capturePerspective`, `captureScope: 'window'` | `src/ai/client/DockService.mjs:282` | records the holder's perspective document when the holder offers one | `readDocument(holder)` for a holder without the read | JSDoc | unit arm |
| `getDockZoneDocument()` | `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs:2312` | unchanged: the live committed document | — | — | existing arms |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A window-scope capture taken while a pane is in a vessel places that pane in its recorded home, at the recorded index (`WorkspaceDocument.findContainingTabsId` on the record is not null).
- [ ] The read changes nothing: `dockModel` is the same value before and after, no history row, no projection.
- [ ] The record equals the document the pane's real return leaves — for an intact home, a home that collapsed with the detach, and a recorded home that resolves to nothing (the host's no-home answer).
- [ ] A pane the document already places while it is away is recorded where the document has it.
- [ ] A fold the reducer refuses leaves the record as the live document has it, and the capture still succeeds.
- [ ] Topology-scope capture is unchanged.
- [ ] The arm for the first criterion is red on dev.

## Out of Scope

- The restore side. Re-seating every unplaced catalog item after a restore would reopen panes a perspective closed on purpose — placement is what a perspective reveals.
- The cockpit's own capture verb moving to the new read: neomjs/neo-agent-institution#127, on the pin that carries this.
- Records captured before this lands.

## Avoided Traps

- Folding inside `getDockZoneDocument()`: it is the dock-holder contract's live read (topology diffs, operation results), and a folded answer there would describe a document nobody committed.
- A fold in each host's capture verb: every host with tear-outs would re-derive it, and the Neural Link capture would still record the hole.

Decision Record impact: none.
